sentences.text: Shamosaurus was a medium-sized, herbivorous basal ankylosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Early Cretaceous.
Its skull roof lacked pronounced, separated head tiles, though it featured short, slightly rounded horns at the rear corners.
The animal possessed a sharp, toothless upper beak that angled forward and was protected by two cervical halfrings, each containing six segments.
Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated the creature measured 5 meters in length and weighed 2 tonnes in 2010.
Later, Mark Holtz suggested the species could have reached 7 meters long in 2012.

A Soviet-Mongolian expedition uncovered the first ankylosaur skeleton in the Lower Cretaceous of Mongolia in 1977, leading Tatyana Tumanova to name and describe the species Shamosaurus scutatus in 1983.
The holotype fossil, which dates to about 115 million years ago and originates from the Dzunbain Formation, includes a complete skull, lower jaws, and a partial postcranial skeleton with armor.
Tumanova originally classified Shamosaurus within the family Ankylosauridae and established the subfamily Shamosaurinae.

A 2014 phylogenetic analysis by Victoria Arbour identified Shamosaurus as the sister species of Gobisaurus, while recent analyses suggest it belongs to Shamosaurinae or is a more derived ankylosaurid than Gobisaurus.
Shamosaurus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
